learning: If s-bend and slalom line-loss falls to about 1.0 or below with max_error under 0.06 m, turn authority was the gap. If line-loss stays at 1.4 or more, the gap is the controller's response on sharp bends, and the next change should be weights, not geometry. If oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 with low max_error, that is a weight problem.
notes: Builder's iteration 5 geometry (iteration 4 with wheel_track narrowed from 0.11 to 0.10 m) paired with the unchanged iteration 4 controller, so only turn authority differs from the best-known result.
rationale: Iteration 4 (y = 0.07 m, score 364.1, the best so far) improved the oval from 13/20 to 16/20 finishes with max_error 0.037 m, but s-bend and slalom were unchanged: 0/20 finishes, line-loss 1.4 and 1.95 per run, and max_error 0.063 to 0.064 m. Forward look-ahead therefore helped the oval but is not the sharp-track gap. Span (iteration 2) and footprint (iteration 3) were both tested and both hurt, so neither is the lever. Speed is not limiting, since the oval completes in about 1.82 s. The remaining untested geometry lever is wheel_track, which sets the turn rate per unit of PWM difference. I narrow wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.10 m, as the Builder requested, and keep the rest of the geometry unchanged, including y = 0.07 m. Iteration 4's controller (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction) is kept unchanged, so this race isolates turn authority. A narrower track adds roughly 10 percent more turn per unit of PWM, so I do not raise kp; I accept the risk of more oval oscillation (0.28 now) and will handle it with weights in a later iteration if it appears. Expected result: s-bend and slalom line-loss falls toward 1.0 or below and max_error drops under 0.06 m, with the oval finish rate held at 16/20 or better.
